_source.description: Major global cadmium production sites — produced almost entirely as byproduct of zinc smelting/refining
_source.origin: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2024 (https://pubs.usgs.gov/periodicals/mcs2024/); International Zinc Association (https://www.zinc.org/); International Cadmium Association (https://www.cadmium.org/); Company annual reports: Korea Zinc, Nyrstar/Trafigura, Hindustan Zinc/Vedanta, Teck Resources, Zhuzhou Smelter Group, Huludao Zinc Industry, Toho Zinc, Mitsui Mining & Smelting, Kazzinc/Glencore, Nexa Resources/Votorantim, Sun Metals/Korea Zinc, First Solar
_source.license: USGS: public domain; company data: fair use summary of publicly reported production figures
_source.notes: Cadmium is produced almost entirely as a byproduct of zinc refining. Global refinery production ~24,000 tonnes/year (2023). China accounts for ~35%, South Korea ~15%, Japan ~10%. Coordinates from USGS MRDS, company technical reports, and satellite verification. Capacity figures are for cadmium metal output in tonnes per annum where available. One entry (First Solar) is a major CdTe consumer, not a producer.

_coverage.known_gaps: Numerous smaller Chinese zinc smelters with cadmium byproduct recovery; Russian cadmium production from Chelyabinsk Zinc and other smelters; Mexican cadmium from Grupo México zinc operations; Namibian Skorpion Zinc refinery

sites.name: Zhuzhou Smelter Group
sites.notes: One of China's largest zinc smelters; major cadmium byproduct producer; Zhuzhou, Hunan Province; integrated zinc-lead smelting complex with multi-metal recovery

sites.name: Huludao Zinc Industry
sites.notes: Major zinc smelter in Huludao, Liaoning Province; one of the largest zinc smelting operations in northeastern China with significant cadmium recovery

sites.name: Shaoguan Smelter
sites.notes: Integrated lead-zinc smelter in Shaoguan, Guangdong Province; multi-metal recovery including cadmium from zinc electrolysis residues

sites.name: Baiyin Nonferrous Group Smelter
sites.notes: Zinc and copper smelting complex in Baiyin, Gansu Province; cadmium recovered from zinc refining circuit; historically one of China's key nonferrous metal bases

sites.name: Zhuji Zinc Smelter
sites.notes: Zinc smelter in Zhuji, Zhejiang Province; cadmium byproduct recovery from electrolytic zinc production

sites.name: Korea Zinc — Onsan Smelter
sites.ownership: Korea Zinc (publicly listed, Young Poong Group affiliate)
sites.notes: World's largest zinc smelter; Onsan National Industrial Complex, Ulsan; processes zinc concentrates from global sources; major cadmium producer via electrolytic zinc refining; also recovers numerous minor metals

sites.name: Young Poong — Sukpo Smelter
sites.ownership: Young Poong Group (private, Korea Zinc affiliate)
sites.notes: Zinc smelter at Sukpo, North Gyeongsang Province; cadmium recovered as byproduct of zinc electrolysis; Korea's second-largest zinc producer

sites.name: Akita Zinc Smelter
sites.notes: Zinc smelter in Akita Prefecture, northern Honshu; cadmium recovered from electrolytic zinc refining; operated since 1965

sites.name: Mitsui Mining & Smelting — Kamioka
sites.ownership: Mitsui Mining & Smelting (publicly listed, Mitsui Group)
sites.notes: Historic Kamioka mine and smelting complex, Gifu Prefecture; zinc smelting with cadmium byproduct recovery; also site of Super-Kamiokande neutrino detector in former mine workings

sites.name: Toho Zinc — Annaka Smelter
sites.notes: Zinc smelter in Annaka, Gunma Prefecture; cadmium and indium recovery from zinc concentrates; one of Japan's three major zinc smelters

sites.name: Teck — Trail Smelter
sites.notes: Integrated zinc-lead smelter in Trail, British Columbia; one of the world's largest zinc refineries; cadmium recovery from zinc electrolysis purification step; operating since 1906

sites.name: Canadian Electrolytic Zinc (CEZinc)
sites.notes: Electrolytic zinc refinery in Salaberry-de-Valleyfield, Quebec; cadmium recovered during zinc purification; capacity ~265,000 tpa zinc

sites.name: Kazzinc — Ust-Kamenogorsk Smelter
sites.notes: Integrated zinc-lead smelting complex in Ust-Kamenogorsk (Öskemen), East Kazakhstan; cadmium recovered from zinc electrolysis; also operates gold refinery

sites.name: Nyrstar — Port Pirie Smelter
sites.notes: Multi-metals smelter in Port Pirie, South Australia; primarily a lead smelter with zinc and cadmium recovery; one of the world's largest primary lead smelters; recently upgraded with new TSL furnace

sites.name: Sun Metals — Townsville Refinery
sites.notes: Zinc refinery in Townsville, Queensland; cadmium recovered as byproduct of electrolytic zinc production; capacity ~200,000 tpa zinc; powered partly by on-site solar farm

sites.name: Hindustan Zinc — Chanderiya Smelter
sites.notes: Zinc-lead smelter complex at Chanderiya, Chittorgarh, Rajasthan; cadmium recovery from zinc purification; part of Hindustan Zinc's integrated zinc-lead-silver operations; largest zinc producer in India

sites.name: Hindustan Zinc — Dariba Smelter
sites.notes: Zinc smelter at Dariba, Rajsamand district, Rajasthan; newer smelter in Hindustan Zinc's complex; integrated with Dariba mine; cadmium byproduct from zinc electrolysis

sites.name: Nyrstar — Balen-Wezel Smelter
sites.notes: Electrolytic zinc smelter in Balen, Antwerp province, Belgium; cadmium recovered during zinc purification; capacity ~280,000 tpa zinc; one of Europe's largest zinc smelters

sites.name: Nyrstar — Budel Smelter
sites.notes: Electrolytic zinc smelter in Budel-Dorplein, North Brabant, Netherlands; cadmium recovery from zinc electrolysis purification; capacity ~260,000 tpa zinc

sites.name: Cajamarquilla Zinc Refinery
sites.ownership: Nexa Resources (publicly listed, Votorantim S.A. majority)
sites.notes: Zinc refinery near Lima, Peru; one of the largest zinc refineries in the Americas; cadmium recovered as byproduct; capacity ~340,000 tpa zinc; processes concentrates from Peruvian mines

sites.name: First Solar — Perrysburg Manufacturing
sites.notes: Major consumer of cadmium telluride, NOT a cadmium producer; included for supply chain context; headquarters and manufacturing facility in Perrysburg, Ohio; world's largest thin-film solar manufacturer; operates closed-loop CdTe recycling program

sites.name: Padaeng Zinc Smelter
sites.notes: Zinc smelter in Tak Province, Thailand; electrolytic zinc production with cadmium recovery; capacity ~100,000 tpa zinc; sources concentrates domestically and from imports
